title: H362 — HMM + RL Regime Allocation on SPY/TLT/GLD (arXiv:2605.27848)
description: Add a reinforcement-learning allocation policy on top of the 3-state Gaussian HMM regime detector from H251. H251 tested SPY/TLT/GLD with a 3-state HMM but used static regime-conditional weights (OOS Sharpe 0.941). arXiv:2605.27848 (Verma et al., May 2026) applies an RL policy over the same 3-state HMM on 2004-2025 SPY/TLT/GLD data and achieves Sharpe 1.68 vs static 0.92 — a 1.83× improvement. The RL policy dynamically adjusts within each regime state rather than applying fixed weights. Hypothesis: replacing H251's static regime-conditional weights with an RL-trained policy improves OOS Sharpe beyond the H311 EW-4 gate (1.532).
rationale: H251 was CONFIRMED with OOS Sharpe 0.941 but noted the HMM behaved as near-static 80/10/10 allocation. The limitation was static weights, not the regime detector. RL policies can learn non-linear allocation rules within each regime that static weights cannot. The paper uses PPO or similar RL algorithm; our implementation can use stable-baselines3 (already installed). The 3-asset universe (SPY/TLT/GLD) matches H251 exactly — no new data infrastructure needed. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.532 (H311 EW-4+VIX benchmark), MaxDD < -10%.
notes: Start with the H251 HMM regime labels as features; add daily returns, VIX, yield curve as additional state inputs. RL episode = 1 year; reward = risk-adjusted return. Train on IS; freeze policy for OOS evaluation. Do NOT re-train in OOS.
